title: False promise to marry as rape - how courts test 'consent'
p1:
A promise to marry can become a criminal offence. But does every failed relationship become a crime?

This is where courts draw a difficult line between a broken promise and a false promise made with dishonest intent.
p2:
A common misconception is that if a marriage does not happen, consent automatically becomes invalid. That is not how courts examine these cases.

The key question is often: Was the promise genuine when it was made, or was it only a tool used to obtain consent?
p3:
Courts look at the circumstances around the relationship, including the accused person's intentions from the beginning and the facts showing whether the promise was made in good faith or through deception.

The legal test is not about punishing every failed relationship. It is about identifying whether consent was obtained through deliberate fraud.
conclusion: Should the law focus more on the intention behind the promise, or on the outcome when a relationship ends?
